# F8 · Assistant Overview — the week in one read

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F8-AC-01` – `F8-UP-03`.

#### F8 · Assistant Overview — the week in one read

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** The entry screen for the week — F3 and F4 calls, F5's chip plan and F6's refresh are all reached from here. |
| Serves | The first core job in Section 2.3 — decide, without fresh manual research every deadline — and its stated differentiator: a squad-state disclosure line and a stated confidence figure on every call, both surfaced here first. |
| Happy path | The manager opens the Assistant tab. A scrolling column shows an editorial card in the assistant's voice, a squad widget, then every outstanding call as a card grouped by category; opening a card leads into its call (F3/F4), or, for a category with everything decided, into Category Cleared. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F8-AC-01** | The editorial card states four things, always — the four criteria below. It never states fewer, and a quiet week is stated rather than left blank (F3-UP-04). |
| **F8-AC-02** | The editorial card states the decided count, in individual calls rather than categories ("3 of 7 calls decided"). |
| **F8-AC-03** | The editorial card states a priority tally by conviction band with the **forced count first** — the forced figure reads the call's forced property, never a conviction threshold — then the band words in their ramp colours. |
| **F8-AC-04** | The editorial card states one line naming the squad state the week's calls were built from — either "built from your squad as at the GW2 deadline" or "built from the squad screenshots you uploaded at 18:12" (see F2). This line is what makes Section 2.3's freshness-disclosure differentiator true; without it the claim would have to be dropped. |
| **F8-AC-05** | The editorial card states a one-line flagged-player summary ("3 · flagged: Muñoz out, Semenyo 50%, Isak 75%") that opens the news-alert token's tooltip rather than repeating the detail inline. |
| **F8-AC-06** | The tally, the headline call count and the flagged summary all derive from one list of the week's live calls and one list of flagged players, so no two of them can disagree. |
| **F8-AC-07** | **In a blank or double gameweek the editorial must lead with it and state the consequence** — that bench order becomes the most important substitution in a blank week (F3-AC-06), and that a double is when the chip plan matters most (F5). |
| **F8-AC-08** | **The editorial's own prose is exempt from the Voice constraint's two-sentence rule (3.4).** It is the week in one read — a synthesis across every call — and is clamped to five lines with a MORE / LESS control. Its tone is still bound by that constraint: plainly stated, taking a position, no hedging. |
| **F8-AC-09** | A squad widget shows two mini pitches labelled Before and After. |
| **F8-AC-10** | The squad widget carries three totals — projected points net of any points hit, **NBal** for the scenario on screen (3.1 Terms; not the same number as the status bar's NBal unless the active filter is Selected), and free transfers used against the allowance — all three recomputed for whichever filter chip is active. |
| **F8-AC-11** | The squad widget's free-transfer figure turns red and states the deduction ("FT 2/1 · −4 pts") when the scenario exceeds the allowance. |
| **F8-AC-12** | The refresh control for this screen sits in the Assistant status bar (3.1) and is scoped to every category at once, labelled ALL (see F6). |
| **News alert token** |  |
| **F8-AC-13** | **A red token in the Assistant status bar carries the count of squad players whose evidence has moved since the last successful run** — an availability flag, the news line, a chance-of-playing figure or a price, as diffed by F6. |
| **F8-AC-14** | The token is the only thing in the product that tells the manager the world has moved. Without it, Section 2.3's second customer job depends on him guessing when to refresh, which is the failure that job exists to remove. |
| **F8-AC-15** | Tapping the token opens a tooltip naming each flagged player with a one-line verdict in the assistant's voice ("Isak — expected to start at 75%, keep him in the team") and a refresh action. |
| **F8-AC-16** | That refresh action always runs at every scope, because new team news is squad-wide; a scoped run must never half-clear the token. |
| **F8-AC-17** | The token clears only when a run consumes the news. |
| **F8-AC-18** | While the token shows, the status bar's last-run line reads "last run 19:41 · 3 players flagged since" and the refresh confirmation's subline says the same. Once consumed, both read "squad news up to date". |
| **F8-AC-19** | The token never fires a run on its own, and its presence never refreshes anything automatically (F6-AC-15). |
| **Filter Chips** |  |
| **F8-AC-20** | **All.** Every outstanding call, forced or not. |
| **F8-AC-21** | **Forced Only.** Calls the manager has no real choice about (see Forced, 3.1 Terms). |
| **F8-AC-22** | **Forced and Recommended.** Forced calls plus Recommended ones — conviction of 80% or higher, the *strong* and *certain* bands (see Recommended, 3.1 Terms). |
| **F8-AC-23** | **Selected.** Only the calls the manager has actually accepted so far — his own decisions, not the assistant's advice. |
| **F8-AC-24** | All, Forced Only and Forced and Recommended are three views of the assistant's own advice, unfiltered by what has been decided; Selected is the one filter that reflects the manager's choices instead. |
| **F8-AC-25** | **Under a band filter the After squad and its totals mean "if you took the advice" — including the calls the manager rejected.** The band filters are read-only views of the advice as given, so a rejected call still belongs to its band and the original recommendation stays inspectable. This is the counter-intuitive half and must be stated on screen, not inferred. |
| **F8-AC-26** | A rejected card under a band filter still carries its rejected state and its reduced opacity, so it is never mistaken for one he has not touched. |
| **Call Cards** |  |
| **F8-AC-27** | Below the squad widget, every outstanding call is shown as a card, grouped into three categories in this order: **Transfers** (meta: count suggested), **Substitutions** (meta: count suggested), **Captain** (meta: *"1 pick · 1 held"* when the vice is held, otherwise *"2 picks"* — the armband and vice-armband calls share this one category rather than splitting into a fourth). |
| **F8-AC-28** | Each call card is two adjacent panels with a visible seam — a content panel that opens the call's detail (Head to head, F3/F4), and a decision panel that decides it in place — so a decision button never sits inside a fully tappable card. |
| **F8-AC-29** | **Each card's decision panel has three states.** *Undecided:* three tappable actions — Select, Reject, Later — matching F3's swipe gestures. *No real choice available:* a fixed "No change" or "Nothing to do" reading, not an editable panel. *Already decided:* a status pill plus a "Change" control that reopens the decision panel in place. |
| **F8-AC-30** | Changing a decision from the card's own panel, and how a rejected card renders, follow F3-AC-10 and F3-AC-11; they are not restated here. |
| **F8-AC-31** | **Each call card carries a small fixture chip beside its flag** — *×2* in green, or *BLANK* in grey with a dashed border — whenever a player on either side of the call has two fixtures or none this gameweek, so an exceptional week is visible without opening the call. |
| **F8-AC-32** | **A category can hide items under the active filter chip.** When it does, the category ends with a dashed row stating how many are hidden, plus a "Show all" link that clears the filter back to All. |
| **F8-AC-33** | A filter hides; it never recolours a card, because the border already carries conviction and opacity already carries decisions. |
| **Below the Call Cards** |  |
| **F8-AC-34** | **A Chips section, hardcoded rather than filtered.** Header "Chips" with a "season plan" meta, and one clickable preview row summarising the plan's current state (for example "Bench Boost → GW7 · plan holds") that opens the Chips tab (F5). |
| **F8-AC-35** | **Footer hint, always present:** small centred caption text reading "Tap a call for the full evaluation." |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F8-UP-01** | **A refresh run fails.** Acceptance: the overview keeps the previous advice intact rather than clearing it; see F6's Run failed state. |
| **F8-UP-02** | **Every call in a category is decided.** Acceptance: that category's tab meta reads *Done* and Category Cleared is shown instead of an empty list; returning from there comes back to the overview. |
| **F8-UP-03** | **FPL's data feed is unreachable.** Acceptance: see F6 — the overview works from the last read and states how old it is. |
